description: Per-job fault triage for IREN_MKZ GB300. Canonical owner of per-job GPU and host fault counters. Placement, resource totals and per-GPU detail live on Job Stats.

options.content:
Job Health — where did it break?

Fault triage for the selected Job ID. The job's tray set comes from cgroup_info (Slurm cgroup exporter), then every GPU and host series is restricted to those trays. Each tile's exact entities are in the table directly beneath it, built from the same selector — the number on the tile is that table's row count. Placement and resource totals live on Job Stats. Silent means no sample for over five minutes, measured from the last sample timestamp — not up==0, which never fires here because a dead tray loses its scrape target instead of reporting zero.

panels.title: Is the job computing, or stalled on communication?

panels.description: Averaged over every GPU on this job's trays. A high SM clock with near-zero memory-copy utilisation means the GPUs are spinning without moving data — the classic signature of a collective stalled on communication. Per-GPU power, utilisation, temperature and framebuffer live on Job Stats, which owns that dataset.
panels.title: Is the job computing? — SM clock and memory-copy utilisation, job average
GPU faults on this job's GPUs — the exact GPUs are in the table under each tile

panels.description: DCGM exports DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS only while an XID is latched on the GPU, so the presence of the series is the fault.

targets.expr: count(DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS and on(instance) max by(instance)(last_over_time(cgroup_info{cluster=~"$cluster",jobid=~"$jobid"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Trays of this job on which the kernel OOM killer fired inside the dashboard range — the most common cause of a rank vanishing.

targets.expr: count(sum by(node)(increase(node_vmstat_oom_kill[$__range]) and on(instance) max by(instance)(last_over_time(cgroup_info{cluster=~"$cluster",jobid=~"$jobid"}[$__range]))) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Trays of this job that stopped answering telemetry: their newest node-exporter sample inside the dashboard window is more than 5 minutes old. This is measured as sample staleness, NOT as up==0 — on this stack a tray that dies has its scrape target removed, so up==0 never fires and an up-based tile would read 0 while a whole rack is dark. The table beneath names the exact trays and how long each has been silent.

targets.expr: count(min by(node,rack,su)((time() - tlast_over_time(up{job=~"node|node-exporter"}[$__range])) and on(instance) max by(instance)(last_over_time(cgroup_info{cluster=~"$cluster",jobid=~"$jobid"}[$__range]))) > 300) or vector(0)

defaults.noValue: None — every tray of this job is answering
